messages:
jordan: Quick sync — thinking about normalizing tenant signals at ingress so the dedicated operator can be agnostic to per-tenant QPS semantics. We keep operator simple: only consumes a fixed signal vector. Thoughts?

alex: I like that. Operator complexity has been growing trying to special-case every tenant. +1 for a small, well-documented vector.

maria: wary of losing important characteristics (burstiness, tail latency, retry storms). If we squash too much into a single score we lose options for smart prewarm.

jordan: agree — proposal is a 3-field vector: steady_rps, burstiness (0-1), recent_tail_ms. Operator maps those to admission actions (prewarm / queue / deny) via a policy table.

sam: practical question: who normalizes? LB ingress or tenant agent? We need the signal to be trustworthy; tenants can lie about steady_rps if untrusted.

jordan: normalization should be done server-side in the fronting proxy (ingress). We have access to real request pacing and can compute rolling windows.

alex: sketch of wire format: 
```yaml
admission_signal:
  steady_rps: "12.4"
  burst_score: "0.67"
  tail_p95_ms: "420"
  sample_window_s: "30"
```
Operator accepts that as a JSON blob and applies a configurable mapping.

maria: mapping needs to expose hysteresis params. We burned CPU oscillations last quarter from tight thresholds. If operator decides prewarm, it must hold credits for a cooldown.

sam: +1. Also we should include a "signal_confidence" flag so operator can fall back to conservative behavior if ingress is noisy.

jordan: how minimal should operator semantics be? Option A: operator makes admission decisions directly. Option B: operator translates signal to tokens/credits and leaves decision to downstream admission controller. I prefer B for separation of concerns.

alex: B scales better — operator becomes a translator and credit ledger. Admission controller (closer to scheduler) applies policy for evictions and per-request admission.

maria: does that imply two separate controllers? one for credit issuance and one for per-request admission? We already have the shard allocator — adding another hop increases latency.

jordan: not necessarily separate processes — logical separation but co-located. The important bit is API boundary and responsibilities.

sam: fallback policy question: if credits exhausted, should we autoscale up nodes or degrade to hosted fallbacks? For tenants with enterprise SLA we should favor scale-up; for free-tier prefer graceful denial.

alex: that means operator needs tenant metadata (tier + SLA) — ingress should attach tenant_profile: {tier: "enterprise" | "standard" | "free"}. Keep it small.

maria: can we avoid exposing raw tenant id? just profile. Privacy and multi-tenancy concerns.

jordan: agreed — attach profile only.

infra-bot: created ticket <https://tracker.redwood.ai/INF-5421|INF-5421> "Ingress signal normalization + operator credit ledger RFC" and added labels: eng-runtime, autoscale, rfc.

alex: action items from thread: 1) Draft RFC with wire format + policy table examples 2) Prototype normalization in proxy (30s window) 3) Add signal_confidence and tenant_profile fields 4) Define operator cooldown semantics for prewarm credits.

maria: volunteers: I'll own cooldown semantics and hysteresis tests.

sam: I'll prototype the proxy normalization patch.

jordan: I'll start the RFC doc and link INF-5421. Can we get a quick sync tomorrow 11am to align on thresholds?

alex: fine with me. If folks want, drop proposed thresholds in the RFC and we'll iterate.

maria: :thumbsup:

jordan: thanks everyone — keeping the operator boundary small should help future refactors and reduce cascading complexity.
